svg.title: authlint demo
svg.desc: Terminal recording: authlint audits a weak OAuth provider, a leaking JWKS and risky client registrations, then a hardened provider that passes and a SARIF export for CI.

text.tspan: AL102 Endpoint is not served over HTTPS
fix: Serve every endpoint over TLS; tokens and codes sent over plain HTTP can be stolen.
AL104 Resource owner password grant is enabled
grant_types_supported includes password, so clients handle user credentials directly.
fix: Disable the password grant; the security BCP says it MUST NOT be used.
Supported: id_token token, token. Access tokens are returned in the URL, where they leak through
fix: Remove response types that contain 'token' and use the authorization code flow with PKCE.
AL107 Unsigned (alg none) tokens or requests are accepted
fix: Remove none so every token or request has to be signed.
AL106 PKCE plain method is allowed
code_challenge_methods_supported includes plain, which sends the verifier in clear.
AL108 request_uri can make the server fetch arbitrary URLs
The metadata does not set request_uri_parameter_supported, which defaults to true in OpenID Connect
Discovery. If request_uri is accepted, the server may fetch any URL a client sends.
fix: Set request_uri_parameter_supported to false if you do not use it, or
AL109 No mix-up defence (iss in authorization responses)
fix: Return iss in authorization responses (RFC 9207) so clients using several providers can detect
AL110 No sender-constrained access tokens (DPoP or mTLS)
Neither DPoP (RFC 9449) nor certificate-bound tokens (RFC 8705) are advertised, so a stolen access
fix: Offer DPoP or mTLS-bound access tokens, at least for high-value APIs.
AL111 Dynamic client registration is exposed
fix: Confirm that registration requires an initial access token, or that open registration is
AL201 Private or symmetric key material is published
keys[1] (kid 2026-main) publishes private key members d. Anyone can use it to forge tokens.
fix: Remove the key, rotate it immediately and publish only public members (kty, n, e or crv, x, y).
AL201 Private or symmetric key material is published
keys[2] publishes a symmetric secret (k). Anyone can use it to forge tokens.
fix: Remove the key, rotate it immediately and publish only public members (kty, n, e or crv, x, y).
AL202 RSA key is shorter than 2048 bits
fix: Use RSA keys of at least 2048 bits, or move to EC (ES256) or Ed25519 keys.
AL203 Keys cannot be told apart (missing or duplicate kid)
Several keys are published and at least one has no kid.
fix: Give every key a unique kid so verifiers pick the right key during rotation.

g.text: authlint client examples/clients.json --fail-on critical; echo exit=$?

text.tspan: AL301 Redirect URI uses plain HTTP
http://app.example.com/callback sends authorization codes over plain HTTP.
fix: Register an https redirect URI.
AL302 Redirect URI contains a wildcard
https://*.example.com/callback contains a wildcard, so codes can be redirected to unintended hosts or
fix: Register every redirect URI exactly; the BCP requires exact string matching.
AL305 Client credentials grant without client authentication
batch-job can use client_credentials with token_endpoint_auth_method none, so anyone who knows the
fix: Authenticate the client (private_key_jwt or tls_client_auth preferred).
AL304 Client uses a grant the security BCP forbids
fix: Switch to the authorization code flow with PKCE.

g.text: authlint provider examples/strong-provider.json && echo 'clean: CI passes'
authlint provider examples/weak-provider.json -F sarif -o authlint.sarif; echo exit=$?
